clue.text: Even better item worn on the head

parts.note: even means level or flat
to better something is to cap it, as in capping a story

explanation.surface: Someone praises a garment as even better than the last thing worn on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb here: to cap a joke is to better it.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft peaked hat, typically tweed, is a classic piece of British headgear.

definitions.meaning: in Genesis Adam was the very first human being created
in grammar, I is the pronoun of the speaker, as opposed to you or he

explanation.surface: Two names paired, as though a person introducing themselves alongside a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings of one phrase: the earliest human, and the grammatical category of the word 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblically Adam was the original human; grammatically 'I' is the speaker's own pronoun form.

parts.note: the head of a queue or procession is its front

explanation.surface: A woman leading something is cast as causing offence.
explanation.definitionFit: To affront someone is to insult them openly, which is to give offence.

parts.note: Cork is a county in Ireland; with the possessive it gives an S
a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: A county side's opening batsman, as in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' reads as a cricketer opening the innings; it is a bottle opener. CORK is a county of the Irish Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is a tool for opening wine bottles, so it is literally an opener.

clue.text: They help mountaineers no end climbing on top of Snowdon

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first part sits above the second
in a down entry, climbing means the letters of no end are read upwards

parts.note: the tip of something is its end

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Climbers on Snowdon, the highest mountain in Wales, scramble up with no end in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns NOTIP into PITON; 'top of Snowdon' gives S, placed below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitons are metal spikes driven into rock to anchor climbing ropes, so they aid mountaineers.

indicators.note: says the opening letter of the word for stop is dropped

parts.note: to cease is to stop

explanation.surface: A traveller asks about a comfort stop, though not the first of the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comfort stop' reads as a toilet break; 'Comfort' is the definition and 'stop' the wordplay. 'not the first' removes C from CEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is a state of comfort, freedom from pain or worry.

indicators.note: the words Science Museum display the answer within their letters, as a museum shows its exhibits

explanation.surface: The Science Museum in London is said to put a bird on display.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird, close kin of the ostrich.

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of seals

parts.note: ling is a long-bodied food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A keeper tosses fish to the seals at feeding time.
explanation.definitionFit: To sling something is to throw or fling it casually, as with a toss.

parts.note: a ref is a referee

indicators.note: backs here means goes backwards, so the word for about is read in reverse

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: A referee directs play involving the defenders, the backs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' looks like the football players; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer someone to a person or place is to direct them there.

clue.text: Sightseer, one in French city close to coast

indicators.note: places the numeral inside the name of the French city

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire in France
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the close of coast is its final letter

explanation.surface: A sightseer in a French city near the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist travels for pleasure, visiting the sights.

clue.text: One leading the way in drift with dog

indicators.note: joins the two words side by side

parts.note: the drift of events is their general trend
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A dog leads its walker along a snowy drift.
explanation.definitionFit: A trendsetter starts fashions that others follow, so leads the way.

indicators.note: says the letter for king is removed

parts.note: took means accepted, as in took the offer
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A deposed king has accepted that he must leave too.
explanation.definitionFit: Too and also are synonyms meaning in addition.

clue.text: Pronounced wickedness, very curious in place of worship

indicators.note: says the words for wickedness and very curious are to be spoken, giving something that sounds like the answer

parts.note: sin is wickedness; agog means eagerly curious

explanation.surface: Marked wickedness and intense nosiness are found, ironically, inside a house of prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like an adjective meaning marked; it signals a sound-alike. SIN AGOG said aloud approximates the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synagogue is a building for Jewish worship.

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper report: an agent shot a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' reads as gunfire; it is the anagram signal, as in 'my nerves are shot'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a giant breed of dog.

clue.text: Complete set of religious books located in Ireland

indicators.note: places the religious books inside the name of the country

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A full collection of religious texts is discovered in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire and complete both mean whole, with nothing missing.

indicators.note: the supply spans across the City, so it goes around it

parts.note: a fund is a supply or stock, as of money
EC is the postcode area of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: Money supplied across London's financial district proves profitable.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the City of London, the financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fecund means fertile or productive, bearing fruit abundantly.

clue.text: Take off something worn in warm weather — not initially

indicators.note: says the first letter is removed

parts.note: a sundress is a light dress worn in hot weather

explanation.surface: Advice to take off a garment in hot weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To undress is to take off one's clothes.

clue.text: Briefly about, American in big top

indicators.note: says the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: circa means about, used with dates
US stands for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: An American is briefly found inside a big top.
explanation.definitionFit: The big top is the main tent of a circus, and stands for the circus itself.

clue.text: Very depressed before this new card game

indicators.note: puts the first pieces ahead of the rest

parts.note: so means very
low means depressed

indicators.note: new means a fresh arrangement of the letters of this

explanation.surface: A player is downcast before taking up a new card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo whist is a variant of whist in which a player may bid to play alone.

indicators.note: the answer is found within the run of letters of Jerusalem once

explanation.surface: A fruit was once discovered in ancient Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is a sour yellow citrus fruit.

clue.text: Scheduled affair of honour? Not quite

indicators.note: says the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: a duel was fought to settle a matter of honour

explanation.surface: A planned duel turns out to be not quite one.
explanation.definitionFit: A train that is due is expected at a scheduled time.

clue.text: Monica worried about daughter moving from place to place

indicators.note: places the rearranged name around the daughter's letter
worried suggests disturbed, so the letters of Monica are rearranged

explanation.surface: Monica frets over her daughter, who keeps moving house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns MONICA into NOMAIC; 'about' wraps that around D.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic people have no fixed home and wander from one area to another.

definitions.meaning: slang for enjoy or appreciate, as in 'I really like that music'

explanation.surface: A description of something resembling an archaeological excavation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' seems to mean 'similar to'; it is the verb, in its slang sense of appreciating.
explanation.definitionFit: Dig is slang for appreciate, and is also the usual term for an archaeological excavation site.

parts.note: dept is the shortened form of department

explanation.surface: An expert works in a department that has had its staff cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept means highly skilled, so an adept is an expert.

parts.note: a nag is an old or worn-out horse

explanation.surface: A rider meets an obstacle near a pony.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hidden difficulty or obstacle.

clue.text: Poet, writer on board Queen Elizabeth

indicators.note: to be on board is to be aboard a ship, so the writer goes inside the vessel named next

parts.note: the liner as a steamship, SS, plus ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A poet writes aboard the liner Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship's name does double duty: steamship prefix plus the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.
